result.result:
The owners are within their right under cp_terms' war risks clause (modelled on BIMCO CONWARTIME 2013): they may decline the Red Sea transit, and charterers (the operator's company) must give other orders by an alternative route, with extra time and bunkers for the charterers' account. Per check_route_change (simulated figures), routing via the Cape of Good Hope from the current position avoids babelmandeb and suez: extra distance 4,800.8 nm, extra time 16 days at 12.5 kn, new ETA at Gijon 2025-02-23T23:00:00Z (+373 hours on the planned 2025-02-08T10:00:00Z). VLSFO on board (about 1,451.6 t) covers the route: about 894.5 t needed, about 557.1 t remaining on arrival, above the 3-day reserve of 80.4 t — no bunker shortfall. check_notices says an ETA notice is now due (ETA moved 383 hours against a 12-hour CP limit), to recipient roles agent and receiver, with the new ETA 2025-02-23T23:00:00Z.

The operator should decide whether to confirm the route change. On a yes: (a) reply to the owners' vessel technical management confirming the route via the Cape of Good Hope; (b) send the ETA notice check_notices says is due to agent and receiver with ETA 2025-02-23T23:00:00Z; (c) propose a voyage management system entry for the port call ETA at Gijon. Recommend nothing be sent until the operator answers.
